transcript:
MEETING HEADER: 2025-07-03 16:00 PDT | Duration: 58m
Attendees: Alex Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Rao (Redwood SE), Jonah Steele (Redwood SE), Marcus Hall (Zenith Head of SecOps), Leah Ortiz (Zenith CRO), Ibrahim Khan (Zenith Platform Eng)

AUTO SUMMARY (auto-generated):
- Goal: Walk through Redwood's incident response, BCDR playbook, RTO/RPO guarantees, SLA and escalation flow for Zenith Payments; validate controls (SOC2/ISO, RBAC/SSO, audit logs, KMS).
- Outcomes: Redwood to share SOC2/ISO artifacts, DR run plan, escalation matrix + PagerDuty template; Zenith to confirm RTO/RPO acceptance criteria and internal stakeholders.

TOPICS: SOC 2 & ISO status; RBAC/SSO provisioning; audit log retention and SIEM integration; encryption/KMS & BYOK; BCDR runbook (RTO/RPO); SLA uptime & credits; escalation matrix & on-call flows; pen test cadence.

TRANSCRIPT:
[00:00] Alex: Hey everyone, thanks for hopping on. we have about an hour. i'll let folks do quick intros. Alex Kim, Redwood account lead.
[00:07] Marcus: Marcus Hall, Head of SecOps at Zenith. we own infra, compliance review.
[00:10] Leah: Leah Ortiz, CRO, i'll be listening for regulatory impact and procurement.
[00:15] Priya: Priya Rao, i look after infra security and DR with Redwood.
[00:18] Ibrahim: Ibrahim khan, platform engineering, mainly on the backup and replication side.
[00:22] Jonah: Jonah Steele, solutions eng, I'll run through the technical playbook details.

[00:30] Alex: Cool. high level, today's agenda is to validate you can meet Zenith's RTO/RPO and escalation needs, make sure audit logs and KMS meet e-discovery and residency, and clarify SLA and what happens if uptime targets are missed. any additions?
[00:40] Marcus: No, that's it. Also want to cover on-call paging and who we escalate to at Redwood. last time it wasn't clear.
[00:45] Alex: good point, we'll map the full escalation ladder.

[01:05] Priya: quick housekeeping — SOC two type II is current through 2025-06, ISO27001 cert in progress but paperwork is available, right Alex?
[01:13] Alex: yep, we have SOC 2 Type II report and the summary redaction-friendly version. ISO certificate is in pending stage but we have the gap-assessment and statement of applicability. I'll attach both.
[01:20] Marcus: great, we need the attestation for our audit board. also do you publish third-party pen test results or a summary?
[01:26] Alex: we publish an executive summary of pentests and the remediation RAG, full reports go under NDA. we'll share the exec sum and the remediation timeline.

[01:38] Ibrahim: on RBAC and SSO — we run SCIM for provisioning and SAML for SSO. we need SCIM user sync and group mapping into Redwood with least privilege roles. what's your provisioning cadence?
[01:46] Priya: Redwood supports SCIM v2 provisioning; groups map to roles. we can do custom role creation for Zenith to match your internal roles. provisioning sync is near-real-time, typically 1-2 minutes depending on SCIM push.
[01:58] Ibrahim: ok that latency is fine. do you keep audit logs of SCIM events?
[02:02] Priya: yes, SCIM and SAML auth events are ingested into audit logs with actor, IP, timestamp, and affected resource. retention configurable — default 13 months. you can export via S3 or stream to your SIEM.

[02:16] Marcus: we require immutable audit logs for 13 months and the ability to stream to our Splunk cluster. is the stream push or pull?
[02:22] Jonah: we support direct push to your S3 bucket with object lock for immutability, and also a Kafka/Syslog connector to stream events to Splunk. we can provide schema and sample exports.

[02:38] Leah: on encryption — we need BYOK and HSM-backed KMS; any customer-managed keys?
[02:44] Priya: yes, we support BYOK with Cloud KMS or customer HSMs on Private deployments. Hosted supports customer-managed keys via partner KMS with bring-your-own-key flow; keys are never exported and all at-rest encryption is AES-256.
[02:58] Ibrahim: what's your key rotation practice?
[03:01] Priya: rotation is customer-controlled for BYOK. if you use Redwood-managed keys, we rotate per industry best practice every 90 days and will provide rotation audit records.

[03:12] Marcus: great. now on to BCDR — we provided our target RTO of 1 hour for critical payment flows and RPO of 15 minutes. how do you meet that?
[03:22] Jonah: for Dedicated/Private we offer cross-region replication and synchronous writes for critical KV caches; for hosted we provide multi-AZ async replication with typical RPO ~5-15 minutes depending on workload. RTO depends on failover automation and warm standbys — we recommend a warm standby with autoscale for critical lanes.
[03:39] Marcus: can you guarantee 1 hour RTO in a contract?
[03:43] Alex: we can offer SLA-backed RTO for Dedicated plans with specific runbooks and runbook drills. Hosted has best-effort with SLA for availability (e.g., 99.9% or 99.95% tiers) and defined failover behavior. We'll include options in the pricing sheet.

[03:56] Leah: what's your SLA uptime target and credit model?
[04:00] Alex: standard hosted SLA is 99.9% with credit tiers. Dedicated customers can get 99.95%+ with custom SLOs and financial crediting. Credits are pro-rated based on downtime windows. we'll attach the SLA matrix.

[04:12] Marcus: important to know escalation windows — if something is degraded, how long before Redwood engages on-call SE vs escalation to engineering?
[04:20] Priya: our standard escalation is: 0-15m initial triage by Redwood support; 15-30m routed to on-call SE (tier 2); 30-60m engaged on-call infra/engineering (tier 3); beyond 60m we invoke executive escalation and war room. For Dedicated customers we do a tighter SLA — SE engaged within 5-10m.
[04:40] Ibrahim: are these timelines contractual or operational? we need them contractual for our vendor review.
[04:44] Alex: we can put the tighter windows into a Dedicated contract addendum. Hosted will be operational commitments.

[05:00] Marcus: walk us through an incident playbook example — say a KV cache corruption affecting authorization validations causing transaction failure.
[05:08] Jonah: step1 detection: alert from telemetry & healthchecks, automatic mitigation: failover to previous snapshot within RPO window, if failover fails escalate to on-call SE, runbook contains commands to roll back model or routing to a read-only cache, execute postmortem and remediation. We maintain snapshots every 5-15 minutes for critical caches.
[05:24] Ibrahim: snapshots every 5-15 min — is that configurable? and do you replicate snapshots cross-region?
[05:29] Priya: configurable per-customer. cross-region replication of snapshots is supported for Dedicated, and for Hosted you can enable cross-region backups with additional retention.

[05:40] Marcus: what about testing — how often do you do DR runs? we want quarterly full failover tests with customers.
[05:47] Alex: we run internal DR exercises quarterly; we support customer-driven DR runs on Dedicated with a joint runbook. we can schedule a full failover drill with Zenith — we recommend a staging run then a production-simulated run.

[05:58] Leah: who is in the war room? we need names and escalation SLAs from Redwood.
[06:04] Alex: primary contact is the AE (me) for business-level comms, SE on-call (Priya/Jonah) for technical triage, and an engineering lead reachable for tier-3 escalation. we'll provide a named matrix for the contract.

[06:18] Ibrahim: re: auditability — for forensic investigations, do you offer point-in-time exports of logs and replay capability?
[06:24] Jonah: yes. we provide point-in-time log exports, request-based replay for sequence of events, and chain-of-custody packaging for legal needs. Exports can be delivered to Zenith's S3 with integrity checks.

[06:38] Marcus: we also require timezone and residency controls — payments data must stay in EU for EU customers. how is regioning enforced?
[06:45] Priya: customers can pin data region per project. for Hosted, we have EU-only tenancy options routed to EU regions. Dedicated/Private allows full VPC control and on-prem options for air-gapped needs.

[06:58] Leah: legal will ask about data deletion and e-discovery hold. what's your process?
[07:02] Alex: we support legal hold via retention policies; deletion is a two-step confirmable process and audit logged. we can freeze deletion for particular tenant IDs on request.

[07:14] Marcus: what about notification windows — are you required to notify customers within X hours for a breach?
[07:20] Priya: Redwood's security incident notification policy is 72 hours post-detection for data breaches with personal data. for high-severity incidents affecting availability we'll notify within 1 hour per SLA commitments for Dedicated customers.

[07:36] Ibrahim: does Redwood integrate with our PagerDuty? we want automatic page creation for severity 1 incidents.
[07:41] Jonah: yes, we integrate with PagerDuty and can push alerts using webhooks; mapping severity to escalation policies is configurable. we'll share a sample PagerDuty integration template.

[07:54] Marcus: pen test cadence — you said exec summaries are public, but frequency?
[07:58] Alex: internal pen tests annually plus third-party tests annually. we also allow customers to perform scoped pen tests with coordination.

[08:10] Leah: how do you handle root cause analysis and postmortems?
[08:13] Priya: every Sev 2+ incident has a postmortem with timelines, RCA, remediation plan and owner. we share redacted postmortems with customers for joint incidents.

[08:24] Marcus: can you produce immutable evidence for auditors — like tamper-evident logs and signed artifacts?
[08:30] Jonah: yes, we support object-lock S3 exports and signing of artifacts (SHA256 hashes) with a timestamp authority.

[08:42] Ibrahim: curious about your backup encryption in-transit — are backups encrypted with TLS and encrypted-at-rest using KMS keys?
[08:48] Priya: yes, backups use TLS 1.2+ for transport; at-rest encryption uses AES-256 and keys managed via KMS (customer or Redwood).

[09:00] Marcus: let's talk SLA credits — how are downtime windows measured? by region or tenant-level?
[09:07] Alex: measured per-tenant endpoint availability; for regional outages we'll surface region-level metrics too. credits calculation is per the SLA doc.

[09:20] Leah: if Redwood misses RTO in a Dedicated contract, what's the remedy?
[09:24] Alex: the remedy options include service credits, targeted remediation support, and joint improvement plans; for critical breaches there's an escalation to execs and a formal root cause report.

[09:38] Marcus: are there any single points of failure in the control plane? we want to understand the control plane availability.
[09:45] Jonah: control plane is multi-region with active-passive datastore and active-active API gateways; it is designed to degrade gracefully with routing to healthy regions. Dedicated deployments can choose an isolated control plane for extra resiliency.

[09:58] Ibrahim: for the DR run — what inputs do you need from our side?
[10:02] Priya: we'll need contact lists, test window, representative traffic patterns, acceptance criteria (RTO/RPO), and a runbook owner on Zenith side. we'll draft a template runbook.

[10:12] Marcus: ok let's confirm timelines: we want the runbook draft by 7/10 and a staging test week of 7/21.
[10:18] Alex: noted, we'll aim for that.

[10:25] Leah: on procurement — we'll need pricing for Dedicated plus the addendum that guarantees the RTO and tighter escalation windows.
[10:31] Alex: will provide Dedicated pricing and contract language for the addendum.

[10:40] Marcus: any open questions from Redwood?
[10:43] Priya: do you have an internal list of vendor approvers and legal contacts for NDA and pen test access?
[10:48] Marcus: yes, i'll share those as part of the action items.

[10:56] Jonah: quick note about monitoring — we provide token-level latency traces and SLO dashboards per model route; this helps spot degradation early.
[11:04] Ibrahim: good, SLO dashboards are key. can you feed those into our Grafana?
[11:07] Jonah: yes, we have a metrics exporter and Grafana dashboards.

[11:16] Alex: ok wrapping up — recap of next steps and action items which I'll put into email. any final comments?
[11:22] Leah: no, thanks everyone. good coverage.
[11:25] Marcus: thanks, appreciate the clarity.
[11:28] Alex: we'll follow up with SOC2 docs and the runbook draft. thanks all.

AUTO ACTION ITEMS (end of transcript): Alex to send SOC2 & pen test exec summary; Priya to draft DR checklist; Jonah to share audit log export sample; Marcus to send RTO/RPO acceptance doc.

END OF TRANSCRIPT
